family: Two periodic layers on two different tableaux
hypothesis: K4 is two repeating-key layers, the first on one keyword tableau and the second on a different one (for example KRYPTOS then A-Z), so that the two keys do not add up on any single alphabet.
scope: C = B[+-B^-1(A[+-A^-1(P) + a_(i mod p)]) + b_(i mod q)]; keys a, b any letters; all (p, q) with 7+ checks on the 24 clue letters (every p + q <= 17); Vigenere/variant/Beaufort per layer; ordered pairs (A, B) of different alphabets from A-Z, KRYPTOS and 84 theme-word alphabets, plus 220,232 dictionary keyword alphabets against A-Z and against KRYPTOS in both orders. 778.1M settings, exact propagation, no key guessed.
outcome: Dead in scope: 0 of 575.6M settings pass with 7+ checks (3 shuffled K4s: 0, 0, 0); at 5-6 checks K4 2 vs shuffled 4, 1, 2 (chance level), best K4 reading -7.36 against -5.1 needed; planted 4/4, each the single survivor and read back in full.

family: Cipher letter as a distance through the sculpture's text (skip-count / book-style reading)
hypothesis: Each K4 letter is a count (its place in A-Z or KRYPTOS order) to step on through a text already on the sculpture, and the letter landed on is the plaintext; either from a window that moves a fixed amount per letter or as a running walk.
scope: P_i = T[s + a*i +- d(C_i)] and P_i = T[q_i], q_i = q_(i-1) + a +- d(C_i); 39 texts (K1-K3 plaintexts and ciphertext, cipher panel, tableau panel, Morse, panels joined, panels by columns/back-and-forth/diagonals) x forwards/backwards x every start x a = 0..31 x A-Z/KRYPTOS numbering x both count directions, ring and line; 16,060,464 settings.
outcome: Dead: best 11/24 clue letters where 24 are needed, readings gibberish (controls: 20 shuffled K4s give 9-11; planted 7/7 found at 24/24 and read back). Also: ordinary English can almost never be encoded this way on these texts (0 of 200 messages by either rule on the K1-K3 plaintext or the cipher panel; a walk dies after about 18 letters), so the method is not workable on prose however it is set.

family: Keyword tableau with a non-dictionary keyword
hypothesis: K4 is a Quagmire I, II or III cipher with a repeating or sliding key on a keyword alphabet whose keyword is not in any dictionary (a name, a German word, a misspelling, a short phrase).

hypothesis: K4's key is a list of numbers written with few symbols (digits in base 2-16, clock hours 1-12 or Roman numeral letters), so on the right keyword tableau the 24 key values forced by the clues fall in a small window of consecutive values or on 7 or fewer values, whatever rule the numbers follow.
scope: 666,993 alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms) x 5 layouts x 4 views (C-P, C+P, P-C, -(C+P)) = 13,339,856 settings; smallest circular window of the 24 key values, number of distinct values, cover by windows of 5-16 and by any 2-7 values, digits 0-9 and smallest base for both signs, Roman letters I V X L C D M with the key letter read in A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet; each clue block alone
